title: C644 — Passenger door side impact sensor connector
introduction:
I start with the passenger-door identity in the table, then let the drawing's cavity labels guide me into the circuit rows. The outline is the envelope; the cavity label is the address that gets you to the right connection. Housing Color and wire Color describe different things, so keep those columns in their own lanes.

Use this page to understand the connector record and its service references. The physical viewing side, access steps, test setup and replacement method are outside this sheet. It also leaves the gauge convention and Size and Used codes undefined. Reading the map does not establish an electrical fault or authorize probing.

edits.why: With the drawing upright, the latch outline is above the side-by-side cavities and the housing has unequal side projections. Those features help orient the illustration on the page. I use its printed cavity labels to navigate the pin table, and the accompanying shell-and-harness row to identify which connector record the view belongs to.

Read each Cavity row across as a complete record: circuit identifier, wire color, gauge, function and terminal reference belong together. The function wording distinguishes the sensor-labelled connection from the control-module/sensor-labelled connection. Keep those descriptions literal rather than inventing polarity or assigning a power-and-ground pair.

Use Number to locate a kit's Service Part and Engineering Shell cross-references. A pigtail service listing and an individual cavity's Terminal Part Number identify different items. The gauge entries likewise describe their respective circuit or kit rows. The catalogue gives no selection rule between the listed kits, so a common shell is not proof of interchangeability.
